title: Course: De Excel a Python (con IA)
description: A course for professionals who live in Excel: learn Python and pandas from scratch with real examples from Paraguay. Free masterclass on November 11, 2026.
lead: For professionals who live in Excel and want to stop doing the same manual steps every week. We start from zero, using real examples from Paraguay: guaraníes, VAT, branch offices.
forWho: You build the same Excel reports every week, step by step.
You join spreadsheets with VLOOKUP and pivot tables aren't enough anymore.
You've never written code and want to start with something useful at work.
You want to use AI to write code, and actually understand what it does.
outcomesTitle: By the end you'll be able to
outcomes: Read, clean and join Excel files with Python.
Rebuild your pivot tables and formulas in pandas.
Combine the files from every branch into a single report.
Ask an AI for code, review it and fix it.

syllabusLead: Eight classes. Each one takes something you already do in Excel and does it in Python.

syllabus.title: From spreadsheet to notebook
syllabus.text: What Python is, how a notebook works, and opening your first Excel file with pandas.

syllabus.title: Filter, sort and calculate
syllabus.text: New columns from formulas, filters and sorting. We calculate 10% and 5% VAT on sales.

syllabus.title: Cleaning data
syllabus.text: Extra spaces, dates stored as text, guaraní amounts with dots as separators. Everything that breaks a report.

syllabus.title: Joining tables
syllabus.text: We join sales with the product catalog and the list of branches.

syllabus.title: Summarizing
syllabus.text: Sales by branch and by month, totals and averages.

syllabus.title: Charts and Excel output
syllabus.text: Quick charts, and a formatted Excel file ready to send to whoever needs it.

syllabus.title: Automation
syllabus.text: Read every file in a folder and combine them into one. Monday's report in one click.

syllabus.title: AI as a copilot, plus a final project
syllabus.text: How to ask an AI for code, how to review it, and how to spot when it's wrong. We wrap up with a project on your own data.

datasetNote: We practice with Distribuidora Ñandutí, a made-up dataset for a Paraguayan distributor with sales, products and branches.
